entities.name: Mecca
entities.label: Place
entities.summary: The holiest city in Islam, located in the Hejaz region of western Saudi Arabia. Home to the Ka'bah (the "House of God" within the Masjid al-Haram), Mecca is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad (c. 570 CE), the site of his earliest revelations, and the qibla (direction of prayer) for 1.8+ billion Muslims worldwide. The annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca — one of the Five Pillars of Islam — draws 2–3 million pilgrims each year, making it the largest annual human gathering on Earth. The city's pre-Islamic history as a trading center and the custodianship of the Ka'bah by the Quraysh tribe shaped the social context of Muhammad's mission.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad and the site of his earliest revelations, Mecca played a pivotal role in shaping the Islamic faith and its global spread. The annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca draws millions each year, making it one of the largest human gatherings on Earth.
